newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu must go if charged or convicted - polls.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu must go if charged or convicted - polls.

text.p: A majority of Israelis believe Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must resign if charged or convicted in a corruption scandal, newspaper opinion polls showed on Friday.

A Dahaf poll of 503 adults in the daily Yedioth Ahronoth showed 52 percent believed he should resign if convicted. A Gallup poll of 487 Jews for the daily Maariv showed 52.6 percent believed he must quit and call elections if indicted.

In the Dahaf Institute poll, with a 4 percent margin of error, 52 percent believed he should resign only if convicted, 25 percent now, and 20 percent if and when an indictment is brought against him. Three percent had no response.
The Gallup poll on Thursday, with a 4.3 percent margin of error, asked what Netanyahu should do if prosecutors charged him.

Of those polled, 52.6 percent said he must quit and call elections and 39.3 percent that he must go about business as usual until judges decide the case. The remaining 8.1 percent did not know or did not respond.
Israeli prosecutors have been poring over police recommendations Netanyahu be put on trial in connection with an influence-peddling scandal in the ill-fated appointment of an attorney general.
